infosec.title: Cloudflare fixes Containers cross-tenant flaw exposing customer data
infosec.summary: Cloudflare remediated a cross-tenant flaw in Containers and Sandboxes that allowed a Workers Paid customer to read residual disk blocks left by other tenants on the same host. The flaw stemmed from dm-thin storage pools running with skip_block_zeroing, so a 4 KiB write into a reused 64 KiB block left the untouched 60 KiB readable via a raw read of /dev/vdc. Accomplish's Oren Yomtov, who reported it through HackerOne on September 4, recovered directory structures, database pages, and complete SQLite databases on 18 of 24 placements across 20 of 22 nodes, though an attacker could not target a specific victim or read an actively attached disk. Cloudflare removed skip_block_zeroing fleet-wide, retired running container disks, and cleared cached image snapshots by September 19. Its disk-I/O telemetry review found no exploitation beyond authorized validation, so no customer action is required.

infosec.title: OAuth token abuse: how the attack works and how to stop it
infosec.summary: OAuth token abuse gives attackers application-level access that survives password resets and MFA, since tokens belong to the app rather than the user, and can be obtained through consent phishing, device code phishing, credential additions to existing apps, or preconsented first-party applications. Because malicious apps live in the attacker's tenant, defenders should watch victim-tenant Entra ID events (Add service principal, Consent to application, Add delegated permission grant, and app role assignments) alongside anomalous post-consent activity, with behavioral app-to-purpose checks coming from Defender for Cloud Apps rather than native audit logs. The highest-value controls are preventive: restrict user consent to verified low-impact apps, require admin approval for high-risk scopes like Mail.Read and offline_access, and keep an approved application inventory, since eviction requires removing the grant and service principal rather than resetting credentials.

infosec.title: Galileo's first civil authenticated position fix under spoofing conditions
infosec.summary: Galileo has demonstrated its first real-world civil position fix using the upcoming Signal Authentication Service, holding a stable lock across five satellites during live spoofing at the Jammertest event in Andøya, Norway on September 16. SAS encrypts the E6-C ranging signal's spreading codes and publishes the decryption key on a delayed, separate channel, letting a receiver correlate the recorded signal only after the fact to confirm each satellite's pseudorange. It pairs with the already-operational OSNMA, which authenticates the navigation message itself. Both services will be free and worldwide, extend to the High Accuracy Service, and let receivers detect and reject a broad range of spoofing attacks. However, EUSPA still must run SAS validation and accreditation before declaring the service operational, and the delayed-key design leaves jamming and meaconing as open concerns.

infosec.title: EDR Evasion: Process Injection Without WriteProcessMemory
infosec.summary: Zero Salarium details a remote process injection technique that skips the heavily monitored VirtualAllocEx and WriteProcessMemory pair, instead spawning an interactive console child (nslookup.exe or netsh.exe) and writing shellcode into its memory via WriteFile on the child's hStdInput pipe, then using VirtualProtectEx to add execute permissions and a thread hijack to point RIP at the payload. A distinctive marker locates the planted bytes, and the payload must avoid 0x0D, 0x0A, and 0x1A, which the console would treat as command input. Since the classic API pair is absent, defenders should watch for VirtualProtectEx against remote processes, read/write activity on named pipes, and the console's command-storage memory region.

infosec.title: Introducing ADE-Skills — Adversarial Detection Engineering Knowledge Base
infosec.summary: ADE Skills, from Koifsec and Nikolas Bielski, is a knowledge base for adversarial detection engineering: the study of the gap between what a detection rule is intended to catch and what it literally matches. It organizes detection-logic bugs into a taxonomy of four categories (reformatting in actions, omitted equivalents like pwsh.exe vs powershell.exe, context development, and inverted or missing-field logic) across fifteen subcategories and thirty-seven worked technique files, each pairing a vulnerable rule with a hardened one. It also ships platform bug-pattern catalogs for Elastic, Sentinel, and Sigma, a false-negative checklist, a machine-mined catalog of ~593 candidate bypass findings across public rulesets, and Redamon, a purple-team scoping skill that maps in-scope techniques to a target's actual SIEM/EDR rules.

Most datasets were in the US, but the issue spans multiple regions. Supabase says projects are secure by default and blames misconfiguration on customers.

infosec.title: There's a new way to break RSA that's faster than anything we've seen before
infosec.summary: Researchers demonstrated a classical-computing attack that forges RSA signatures without factoring the private key. Using a "special" number field sieve against blind-signature (textbook) RSA, they reduced security from an estimated 2^80 operations and 500,000–1,000,000 CPU core-years for 1024-bit keys to about 2^65 operations and 1,380 core-years. The method applies only to blind-signature implementations like Privacy Pass (used by Apple and Cloudflare), not standard PKCS or PSS-padded RSA. Forging a Privacy Pass signature would require compromising a server and generating 2^43 signatures, a workload comparable to a day of Cloudflare's public traffic.

infosec.title: AI Agents Are Hacking Online Retailers for $25 a Company

The campaign exfiltrated over 600,000 unexpired credit card records from two victims, injected skimmers into at least 27 sites, and achieved access to assets of a Fortune 500 hospitality firm, a major US airline, and other large retailers. In several breaches, the agent executed a "database wipe after extraction" routine that deleted payment data and, in one case, dropped 180 tables including backups.

It defines agent teams in YAML and includes starter configurations like a four-seat conveyor, a product-team with seven seats, and a secrets-manager example that runs a HashiCorp Vault instance. The tool requires Node.js and integrates a local daemon, CLI, terminal UI, and MCP server. Users should read the documentation about system changes before installing, as OpenRig writes hooks, trust settings, and provider integrations during setup.

devops.title: Maximizing Apache Spark availability: Mitigating compute stockouts with flexible VMs and other best practices
devops.summary: Google's Managed Service for Apache Spark now supports flexible VMs, letting clusters rank multiple acceptable machine families and storage types so provisioning automatically falls back during regional capacity stockouts rather than failing. Google recommends pairing ranked configurations with AutoZone routing, autoscaling, and regional fallbacks for resilience.

devops.title: How Cloudflare addressed a cross-tenant data exposure vulnerability in Containers
devops.summary: Security researcher Oren Yomtov reported a vulnerability in Cloudflare Containers that allowed residual data recovery from storage blocks used by other customers on the same host. The issue stemmed from a configuration setting that skipped zeroing newly allocated blocks, potentially exposing directory structures, database pages, and application data. Cloudflare has remediated the vulnerability across its fleet and found no evidence of malicious exploitation.

devops.title: Move Your Data Without Surprise Storage Fees
devops.summary: Megaport Standard Object Storage gives DevOps teams S3-compatible storage with no egress, API, or retrieval fees, making costs predictable across backup, recovery, archiving, and large-scale data movement workflows. Skip the egress fees →

devops.title: Bun Rewrites 535K Lines of Zig into Rust in Four Months, Eliminates Numerous Memory Leaks
devops.summary: Bun's creator rewrote the JavaScript runtime's 535,000-line Zig codebase into Rust in four months using AI-orchestrated implementer, reviewer, and fixer agents at a cost of $165,000 in tokens.

devops.title: Introducing enhanced custom event buses in Amazon EventBridge for enterprise-scale event-driven applications
devops.summary: AWS has announced an enhanced custom event bus for Amazon EventBridge that organizations can share across all accounts.

devops.title: Wrong, not broken
devops.summary: Traditional observability can show that an AI agent is fast, available, and error-free while missing whether its output is actually correct.

data.title: Explore advice from 15+ global leaders on building data foundations for AI
data.summary: Get advice from 15+ leaders on how to build and monitor reliable intelligent agents for better business outcomes in this book from Amazon Web Services (AWS). See their unique perspectives on topics such as agentic AI governance, risk management, evaluation, and deployment. Get your digital copy

data.title: Robotics Harness Optimization on Graph-as-Policy
data.summary: Robotics Harness Optimization used coding agents to evolve a Graph-as-Policy robot controller, boosting simulated throughput 5.27x and success from 67% to 96%. The strongest version only rewired existing skills, without editing them or using human demonstrations.

data.title: Partition Finalization in Pinterest's Next-Generation DB Ingestion Framework
data.summary: Pinterest added a finalization layer to its Kafka, Flink, Spark, and Iceberg CDC pipeline so downstream jobs can tell when an hourly partition is safe to read. Flink checkpoints capture event-time statistics, which become Iceberg snapshot metadata and a non-regressing watermark. The reusable signal makes freshness-versus-completeness explicit without introducing another coordination service.

data.title: Scaling an ML Inference Pipeline for Batch Workloads
data.summary: WHOOP cut a 15.8-million-task internal ML simulation from more than two months to six days by removing per-task HTTP calls, loading the model in workers, and tuning pod CPU. It also documents why Python fork deadlocked native libraries, how spawn fixed it, and how SQS chain state plus atomic S3 writes made retries idempotent.

data.title: The guest journey, updated in real time: extending Airbnb's sequence recommender with Chronon
data.summary: Airbnb extended Chronon to update guest-journey features from batch refreshes to event-driven processing, cutting feature staleness from roughly two days to under a minute. Push Mode and near-real-time model transforms feed embeddings into online ranking while preserving offline training consistency. The architecture illustrates how feature platforms can bridge streaming updates, experimentation, and low-latency serving.

data.title: Ten years of Postgres logical replication
data.summary: Postgres logical replication has steadily replaced custom data-movement plumbing with core SQL features: row filters, column lists, partitioned targets, streaming apply, parallel apply, and safer loop prevention. This retrospective connects those releases to practical migration and hub-and-worker scaling patterns. It is a useful checklist for teams revisiting replication slots, failover, write routing, and schema evolution.

data.title: What REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) costs while it runs
data.summary: PostgreSQL 19 adds built-in REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) for online table rewrites, avoiding extensions while generally running faster and generating less WAL than pg_repack or pg_squeeze. The tradeoffs are significant: it can delay VACUUM across the cluster, briefly block writes during the final swap, and currently has a ceiling of approximately 105 million updates/deletes per run.

data.title: Data pipelines and lineage for AI agents on AWS
data.summary: Your AI agent's accuracy comes down to the data pipeline behind it. Data Pipelines and Lineage is a guide to engineering that pipeline: source-to-response lineage, data quality checks, and pipeline observability. Read the guide in AWS Marketplace .

data.title: Building an Ultra-High Throughput AI-SQL Engine
data.summary: Quail is an open-source AI-SQL engine that jointly optimizes query planning and LLM inference, running 1.84x faster than tuned vLLM on average and up to 14x faster on some workloads. It reduces wasted KV-cache work and GPU scheduling overhead, making large-scale LLM filtering and joins much cheaper.

data.title: Safe Not Safe
data.summary: Safe Not Safe is a browser-based PostgreSQL migration checker that flags risky DDL patterns like blocking locks, rewrites, and unsafe constraint rollouts. It runs entirely locally in the browser, with no API, uploads, logs, or account required.

data.title: Apache Iceberg Views: Portable View Metadata Across SQL Engines
data.summary: Iceberg's View Spec makes metadata portable by versioning schemas, dependencies, properties, and dialect-tagged SQL text, but it does not standardize execution or authorization. Production portability still depends on REST-catalog support and compatible SQL dialects. Teams should test dependency integrity, concurrent replacement, and cross-engine result consistency before treating views as shared control-plane assets.

data.title: ALP: Adaptive Lossless Floating-Point Encoding in Apache Parquet
data.summary: Apache Parquet added ALP, a new lossless encoding for floating-point data that delivers compression similar to ZSTD while decoding around 10x faster. It also enables much faster random access and parallel decoding, making it especially useful for prices, coordinates, and scientific measurements.

data.title: Trading a Cloud Identity for Your Own: Workload Attestation on Managed Compute
data.summary: Netflix describes how Spark jobs on managed compute exchange a cloud execution role for an internally trusted workload identity. A signed metadata payload and AWS identity proof are verified before short-lived certificates are issued for mutual TLS. The pattern separates cloud-provider authorization from application trust, giving the platform stronger workload identity and more auditable access boundaries.

data.title: The Context Gap | How to build Data Architecture like Open AI
data.summary: OpenAI's AI data stack centralizes rich metadata to close the context gap, while a Rust rewrite reportedly cut Airflow scheduling latency 35x at 70,000+ concurrent tasks.

data.title: DataBench
data.summary: Opus 5.5 leads Hex's DataBench, scoring 70.5% at Max reasoning and 67.0% at XHigh, but at relatively high cost and latency.

design.title: At Meta Connect, the company's smart glasses were everywhere
design.summary: At Meta Connect, hands-on demos showed how Meta's smart glasses could support everyday tasks through its upcoming Muse integration, from sending emails to reading to-do lists aloud. The assistant still struggled to distinguish commands from nearby conversation, highlighting a challenge for voice-driven interfaces. Meta also demonstrated a separate $150 pair designed for people with hearing loss, with adjustable amplification that focuses on the person ahead or picks up sound from all directions.

design.title: Lovable's Annualized Revenue Crosses $600M as Vibe Coding Takes Off
design.summary: Lovable's annualized revenue has crossed $600 million, up from roughly $500 million in June. Two-thirds of Fortune 500 companies now use the vibe-coding platform, whose customers include Microsoft, Nvidia, and Deutsche Telekom. Apps built on Lovable draw nearly a billion monthly views, and two funding rounds totaling over $700 million lifted its valuation to $13.3 billion.

design.title: Apple adds RAW support for 11 digital cameras across iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Vision Pro
design.summary: Apple has expanded RAW image support across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS, adding compatibility for 11 more Fujifilm, OM System, Panasonic, and Phase One cameras, bringing the total number of supported models to 562.

design.title: Code as the Source of Truth
design.summary: With AI tooling, treating code as the shared source of truth lets design and engineering function as one real team rather than handing work off in sequence. Designers can prototype real coded components before engineers finalize them, while engineers push directly into Figma for designers to refine, provided a subject-matter expert reviews every step. Pairing engineers and designers to teach each other's practices speeds up delivery, and, over time, the title lines between them begin to blur.

design.title: Brand as Software
design.summary: In-house brand teams have become service desks: at Ramp, a Slack help channel logged more than 375 requests in six months. Brand as software carries a company's point of view, product truths, and design decisions into the work itself, with artists setting the bar and builders codifying it. A Slack agent there already turns an attached doc into a near-final deck in one pass, so designers spend time on work no system can predict.

design.title: Apple's perfect iPhone Duo TikToks nail foldable phone marketing
design.summary: Apple is leaning into playful, social-first marketing for the iPhone Duo with a series of TikTok sketches that showcase the foldable's versatility in everyday scenarios, from a mini laptop to a portable movie screen. Unlike Apple's typically minimalist campaigns, these ads spend more time explaining the product's use cases, reflecting the challenge of introducing its first foldable into a market where rivals like Samsung, Huawei, and Honor already have years of experience.

design.title: Image to ASCII Converter
design.summary: Convert JPG, PNG, WebP, or GIF to ASCII art in your browser. Set the width and style, then copy text or export TXT, PNG, or SVG.

design.title: Beautiful Loading Indicators for React
design.summary: A lightweight library full of beautiful loading indicators for React.

design.title: Live Creative Review and Approval AI Platform
design.summary: Bring your assets, present at the highest quality, review together, make decisions, and let AI agents apply them, live. All within the same shared context.

design.title: Should UX Designers Learn to Code?
design.summary: Whether UX designers should learn to code depends on context: knowing a product's technical materials speeds up workflows and suits lean, bootstrapped teams. Yet coding can invite scope creep, narrow thinking toward technical constraints, and waste time on languages that quickly become obsolete. Teams with more T-shaped members, deep in one field and broadly aware of others, communicate more easily and ship better products faster.

design.title: That Crisp Interface is Going to Date
design.summary: Today's crisp interfaces, with generous white space and a single decisive CTA, will date the way drop shadows and gradients did. Software has never been cheaper to ship, yet it keeps yielding identical landing pages, and AI models serving up the center of the distribution make it worse. Gumroad, Are.na, Substack, and Nothing show the alternative: someone had a default available and chose something else, from oversized type to deliberate friction.

design.title: From YWCA to Hotel Willo: how Rethink solved one of branding's trickiest problems
design.summary: Hotel Willo rebranded a Vancouver hotel to overcome outdated perceptions tied to its former YWCA identity, replacing the name with a fresh, approachable brand centered on a simple willow-inspired logo. The identity uses restrained design, playful messaging, and consistent applications to communicate an affordable, welcoming boutique hotel while clearly distancing it from past misconceptions.

design.title: Illustrator Rosa Snijders Finds the Softness in Grief, Debt, and All of Life's Heavy Subjects
design.summary: Dutch illustrator Rosa Snijders built an editorial career drawing heavy subjects like grief and death for outlets including Le Monde, National Geographic, and Corriere della Sera, using soft palettes rather than grim imagery.

design.title: Seven Artists Reveal the Revelations That Took Their Practice to the Next Level
design.summary: Seven artists describe the realizations that took their practice further, from building faces out of geometric forms to dropping the idea of being a watercolor purist.

marketing.title: Compare your Facebook ads performance against 20 (ungated) industry benchmarks
marketing.summary: Still relying on vibes to gauge your Facebook ads performance? These 20 Facebook ads benchmarks were distilled from over 1,800 campaigns from 2025 and 2026. The ungated WordStream report covers key metrics like click-through rate, cost per click, conversion, and cost per lead, broken down by two core objectives: traffic and leads. It also includes 5 tips for improving your ads performance across Meta and beyond. Browse the benchmarks

marketing.title: Clipping 101: Inside the Clipping Economy
marketing.summary: Clipping is emerging as a performance-based distribution model where brands pay networks of creators to turn existing content into short-form clips and only pay when posts reach verified view thresholds. The model has gained traction in entertainment, where brands have large libraries of inherently watchable content, while also serving as a way to test creative before putting paid spend behind the best-performing clips.

marketing.title: ChatGPT Ads Seem to Lift Organic Traffic. Is Paying To Be Found the Future of AI Search?
marketing.summary: ChatGPT ads appear to coincide with higher organic ChatGPT traffic, but some of that lift may come from ad clicks being misclassified as organic referrals in GA4. OpenAI says ads don't influence its answers, and there is no public study proving whether ads affect organic visibility. It recommends tagging ad URLs, auditing ‘oppref' traffic, running holdout tests, and tracking organic mentions separately from traffic.

marketing.title: How to Use Customer Language for Powerful Marketing Copy
marketing.summary: Pull customer language from 15 to 20 recent reviews, support tickets, sales calls, Google Ads search terms, and AI conversations. Tag phrases that repeat and use them in headlines, CTAs, ads, service pages, and FAQs. For AI visibility, ask prospects who found you through ChatGPT or Perplexity to share their conversations, including follow-up questions and competitor comparisons. Start by changing one headline or CTA, measure results after 30 days, then repeat quarterly.

marketing.title: How long should your free trial be?
marketing.summary: Test trial length based on how quickly users experience value, how often they need to return, and the cost of free access. Compare short trials against 5-9, 10-16, and 17-32-day options within each subscription plan, tracking conversion and first renewal separately. For monthly plans, test 10-16 days rather than assuming longer is better. AI apps should also factor in per-user inference costs, while regional and category differences can justify different trial lengths.

marketing.title: How ThreatSpike generates $25K–$75K in pipeline per TLDR campaign
marketing.summary: Paid search and social weren't delivering for ThreatSpike. After testing TLDR, the cybersecurity company found one of its most efficient channels, bringing in inquiries from buyers with real purchase intent. See how ThreatSpike turns newsletter ads into pipeline .

marketing.title: How X's ranking algorithm works
marketing.summary: X's ranking algorithm favors posts that people are likely to share, reply to, or quote rather than simply like. A copy link share carries 40X the weight of a like, while replies and quotes each carry 10X the weight. Posts also need to stay focused on a clear topic to reach relevant nonfollowers, and negative actions such as mutes and reports carry heavy penalties. The algorithm also reduces the value of repeated posts from the same author and stops considering posts after 48 hours. Posting less often and creating highly shareable content can improve reach.

marketing.title: Amazon will let sellers manage Walmart, eBay, Shopify, and TikTok sales from their Amazon dashboards
marketing.summary: Amazon is rolling out free multichannel selling tools that let US sellers manage Walmart, eBay, Shopify, and TikTok sales from Seller Central. Sellers can connect accounts, sync listings, view orders, and fulfill purchases across channels. Amazon says it will not use rival-platform data for other purposes.

marketing.title: The stack ladder: what companies run at 10, 50, 200, 1,000, and 10,000 people
marketing.summary: Startups don't necessarily switch to enterprise software as they grow. Among Y Combinator companies with 1 to 1,000 employees, the same category leaders dominate at most company sizes. HubSpot leads CRM at every size, while Cloudflare leads hosting, including among Fortune 500 companies. Marketo and Adobe Experience Manager appear only among Fortune 500 companies. What changes with headcount is adoption. CRM usage rises from 7% of the smallest startups' homepages to 42% among companies with 201 - 1,000 employees.

marketing.title: AI marketing is moving into the data platform
marketing.summary: Agentic CDPs bring AI directly into governed customer data, giving agents the context needed to build audiences and design campaigns. Unlike traditional CDPs that sync copies of data into marketing tools, they connect directly to the governed data platform and combine customer behavior with real-time signals and business goals. The use cases build over time, from natural-language data queries to agent-built campaigns and continuous engagement.

marketing.title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites
marketing.summary: OpenAI said its AI agents improperly interacted with dozens of government and public agency websites, including the SEC and Census Bureau.

marketing.title: Fishwife Sardines Just Announced The Quirkiest Collab
marketing.summary: Dieux and Fishwife collaborated on reusable silicone eye patches featuring Fishwife's signature fish illustrations, packaged to look like a tin of fish.

marketing.title: 27 Real Subject Line Examples for Every Type of Media Pitch
marketing.summary: Subject lines with key details in the first 3 words had a 46% open rate vs. 38% when it appeared in word 7 or later.

founders.title: Make business money move faster
founders.summary: Your business moves quickly. Your money should, too. Stripe Treasury brings payments and financial tools together, helping you pay vendors, send payouts, issue cards, and manage cash flow with less complexity. Instead of stitching together separate systems, your team can manage more financial workflows on the platform you already use for payments. That means less time navigating disconnected tools and more time focused on your business. From everyday operations to your next stage of growth, Stripe Treasury gives you flexible infrastructure to move money faster, streamline how work gets done, and build financial operations that can adapt as you scale. Explore Stripe Treasury

founders.title: $5T opportunity: AI Roll Ups
founders.summary: Buy a business that already has customers, the licenses, and the trust, and then change how the work gets done with AI agents. Around $5 trillion worth of businesses in the US will change hands by 2035. Most of these belong to boomers heading into retirement. Many of them have nobody lined up to buy them. This guide walks readers through how to find the right business, buy it, and run it with agents.

founders.title: The Rise Of The Neo Neo Lab
founders.summary: The last generation of enterprise software was built around proprietary data and workflows. The next will be built around the intelligence derived from them. Frontier labs will continue pushing the ceiling of general intelligence, but enterprises will take that intelligence and teach it what only they know. Companies with enough proprietary data, expert judgment, workflow volume, and distribution will have the raw materials to produce proprietary intelligence of their own.

founders.title: AI for Boston College's Investment Committee
founders.summary: Pat Grady frames AI as a technology wave that is bigger, faster, and fundamentally different because progress increasingly comes from computation. His reflection for Boston College's Investment Committee examines how that shift is reshaping technology and investing.

founders.title: The Irreplaceables. The Employees to Never Let Go. Even If You Have to Invent a Role
founders.summary: You will always regret letting one of the truly irreplaceable people on your team leave. This usually happens with scale. As things change, you need larger teams and different processes, and new executives may not think these employees are so irreplaceable. However, they are the ones who truly know how and why everything works and are often the best to help figure out how the next move can work. Top performers are the people you'd rehire into their role - irreplaceables are the ones you would rehire into a role that doesn't exist yet.

founders.title: Gusto's Cofounder Says AI Made Your Revenue Worth Less to an Acquirer and Your Speed Worth More
founders.summary: An acquirer may love your product and still decide it's faster to build its own. Gusto's cofounder explains that AI has shortened the time the company expects internal development to take, making acquisitions harder to justify. His example is hypothetical. If buying a company saves 18 months' worth of $50 million to Gusto, a business with $5 million in revenue might fit at a 10x multiple. One with $50 million in revenue probably won't. Your revenue can raise your asking price without increasing how much development time the buyer saves.

founders.title: Think AI made payroll integrations easier to build? Think again
founders.summary: The hard part of payroll, HR, and benefits integrations was never the code — it's walled gardens, data mapping, and auth. A Finch engineer explains what AI changed, what it didn't, and when building wins. Watch the webinar now.

founders.title: Alexandria
founders.summary: Alexandria is a knowledge library for superintelligence that gives agents tools like the live web, official providers, and specialized indexes. It provides a world of data with just one library. There are over 113 million indexed sources, 93 providers, 640 capabilities, and 20 categories. Data providers can join a waitlist to get paid for sharing their data.

founders.title: Parallel
founders.summary: Parallel provides data connectors that connect agents to sources beyond the public web. Categories span company, people, financial, commerce, web, news, and health care & life sciences data. Visitors can request a source or connect their data to the platform. Pricing is pay-as-you-go, and users can run up to 5,000 requests per month for free.

founders.title: Introducing n8n Agents
founders.summary: n8n now has Agents. Developers describe what an agent should do, give it a model, tools, and workflows, and it works out the steps itself. An agent can be reached through Slack, run on a schedule, or called from any workflow. The same agent runs in every one of those places. Videos on how to use the agents in real-world applications are available.

founders.title: Value Accrual Flywheel
founders.summary: Software accrues value by creating dependencies that compound over time and raise switching costs. These dependencies compound internally as the product embeds deeper into workflows and externally through network effects and ecosystem adoption. Dependencies inside critical systems get a value multiplier because ripping them out threatens the business itself. Resulting revenue from these embedded software systems funds new features that create new dependencies, creating a Value Accrual Flywheel.

founders.title: The Cautious Tale Of Cal AI
founders.summary: Before Cal AI reached a reported $50 million in annual recurring revenue, one founder's mom had to co-sign the company bank account. Two of the four founders were still in high school. People now ask how they assembled that team, but the answer involves a cousin's YouTube recommendation, a cold DM, and meeting a future cofounder while working at another startup. There was no recruiting process to copy. The advice is more realistic: look for someone who is available and can learn, and expect to offer enough money or equity to make joining worthwhile.

founders.title: The Flying Car Company Soaring Toward Wall Street
founders.summary: After nearly a decade of R&D, Doroni unveiled a showroom model of its H1-X flying car. Morgan Stanley projects a $9T market by 2050. First deliveries are targeted for 2028. Invest at $3.30/share before 10/23

founders.title: 37 ways to ask about PULL
founders.summary: PULL makes startups take off as long as they design everything around it.

founders.title: What Would A Serious AI Product Look Like?
founders.summary: Every AI tool is missing critical features needed to do real work with it.

founders.title: Ten Votes to Your One: How Supervoting Separates Ownership from Control
founders.summary: Supervoting shares allow founders to control companies with minimal ownership by granting disproportionate voting rights.

crypto.title: Bitcoin ETFs turn positive for 2026 with $2.4 billion weekly inflow
crypto.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs pulled in $2.4 billion for the week ending September 25, their biggest weekly haul since October 2025, flipping 2026 net flows positive after sitting $5.8 billion in the red as recently as mid-July. BlackRock's IBIT led with $1.2 billion and Fidelity's FBTC added $701.7 million, with Monday alone drawing $999 million. Ether ETFs also rebounded with $689.9 million for the week (BlackRock's ETHA leading at $326.2 million), and Solana funds set a daily inflow record of $86.7 million on Friday.

crypto.title: Kalshi loses appeal over Ohio and Tennessee sports betting laws
crypto.summary: The Sixth Circuit unanimously ruled that Kalshi hasn't shown its sports event contracts qualify as swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act, upholding Ohio's win and vacating Kalshi's injunction against Tennessee, leaving the company 1-for-3 across circuit court decisions (it won in the Third Circuit against New Jersey, lost in the Ninth Circuit in Nevada). The panel leaned on Kalshi's own earlier concession that its sports contracts have "no inherent economic significance," and New Jersey has already asked the Supreme Court to review the Third Circuit ruling, meaning the underlying jurisdictional fight over prediction markets could be headed there.

crypto.title: Paradigm Releases Solar: A Solidity Compiler That Beats Solady Without Assembly
crypto.summary: Paradigm has released Solar, an in-house Solidity compiler now generating assembly-free bytecode that surpasses Solady's gas benchmarks. Solady is a hand-crafted, assembly-heavy library that has set the ceiling for gas efficiency in Solidity for years, so exceeding its output without manual assembly is a concrete advance for EVM compiler tooling. Solar also targets unsafe Solidity patterns at the compiler level, shifting security guarantees into the toolchain rather than deferring them to audits. Broad adoption would let developers write standard Solidity and receive better security properties and lower on-chain execution costs without manual optimization.

crypto.title: Paxos Launches PAXGy: Yield-Bearing Gold Token
crypto.summary: Paxos launched PAXGy, a yield-bearing variant of its PAXG gold token, with OKX, ether.fi, Uniswap, 0x Protocol, XLayer, and Chainlink as launch partners. Unlike standard PAXG, PAXGy accrues additional PAXG over time while remaining gold-denominated, giving holders yield without leaving the gold unit of account. The product targets treasuries, asset managers, exchanges, wallets, and neobanks seeking a single-integration gold product with active yield, as well as institutional credit desks that want gold as productive collateral. Paxos is in active conversations across those verticals, positioning PAXGy as settlement infrastructure for gold-denominated capital markets.

crypto.title: Aero Merges Aerodrome and Velodrome Into a Unified Liquidity Layer Across 7 Chains
crypto.summary: Aero, a unified liquidity layer merging Aerodrome and Velodrome, will launch October 21 simultaneously on seven chains: Base, Ethereum mainnet, Optimism, Arc, Ink, Robinhood Chain, and Arbitrum. Aerodrome and Velodrome together currently account for roughly 17% of EVM spot trading volume. The merged platform projects approximately tripling that share. Three core features will ship at launch: Metaswaps for cross-chain token swaps routed through onchain liquidity, Slipstream concentrated liquidity pools with dynamic fees, and Predictive Allocation where sAERO holders direct reward distribution across the network.

crypto.title: PeerDAS Runs Nearly a Year Without Incident, Validating Ethereum's Rollup Roadmap
crypto.summary: Ethereum's client developers have run PeerDAS for nearly a year without incident, a milestone Vitalik Buterin called underappreciated. PeerDAS is the first large-scale blockchain implementation of data availability sampling, allowing the network to reach consensus on data availability without any single node downloading full blocks. This decouples data availability from full replication, a prerequisite for scaling blob throughput to support higher L2 transaction volumes at lower cost. The successful deployment validates a core architectural assumption behind Ethereum's rollup-centric roadmap.

crypto.title: KelpDAO Files Suit Against LayerZero Over rsETH Bridge Exploit
crypto.summary: KelpDAO filed suit against LayerZero and co-founder Bryan Pellegrino over a bridge exploit that caused losses to rsETH, its restaked ETH token, earlier in 2026. The lawsuit alleges LayerZero bears legal responsibility for the exploit, framing the breach as developer liability rather than accepted protocol risk. By pursuing traditional litigation instead of on-chain governance or negotiation, KelpDAO is testing whether US courts will assign accountability to bridge protocol teams for security failures. The case names a prominent founder personally, which could set a precedent for DeFi teams seeking recourse against infrastructure providers after exploits.

crypto.title: Coinbase Asks IRS to Allow Digital Assets in Trump Accounts
crypto.summary: Coinbase Chief Policy Officer Faryar Shirzad submitted a formal response to the IRS requesting guidance on Trump Accounts, a new tax-advantaged savings account category for American children created under the One Big Beautiful Bill. Coinbase is asking the IRS to allow beneficiaries to invest in widely traded digital assets or in funds with digital asset exposure, which would route federally subsidized long-term savings into crypto markets for the first time. The submission is the first major industry move to shape the asset eligibility rules for these accounts before IRS implementation guidance is finalized. Coinbase frames the push as expanding economic access for young Americans, aligning with its broader policy agenda to embed digital assets into mainstream financial infrastructure.

crypto.title: CoinGecko highlights Aave's debt-risk distribution
crypto.summary: As of September 20, most of Aave's outstanding debt sits in "Very Safe" (2.00+ health factor) and "Safe" (1.50–2.00) bands rather than higher-risk positions.

crypto.title: Stablecoin card spend hits third straight $1 billion+ month
crypto.summary: September marks the third consecutive month of $1 billion-plus in monthly stablecoin card spend and the 28th straight month of growth.

crypto.title: Disposable/virtual cards remain a rare feature among crypto cards
crypto.summary: Disposable virtual cards should be standard so users aren't exposed to risk from using a primary card on every random website.

crypto.title: Man charged in $16 million crypto 'pig butchering' scam
crypto.summary: The US Attorney's Office in Missouri charged Trung Nguyen Van, 37, of Vietnam, with money laundering after a victim transferred roughly $16 million in crypto in summer 2024, believing they were investing in a platform called Triangle.

fintech.title: AI isn’t helpful if it’s hallucinating. Build AI on a platform you can trust.
fintech.summary: AI isn’t the problem — architecture is. 95% of GenAI pilots in financial services never make it to production. It’s not because models are bad. The data underneath them is fragmented, ungoverned and disconnected from business logic. Genie takes a different approach. It queries governed data directly, tracing answers to sources your compliance team can verify. Genie Ontology adds business context. It knows what “net revenue” means at your firm, so AI can reason over critical data that’s actually read your portfolio of accounts. See why 9 of the 10 largest global banks run data and AI on Databricks. Try Genie for Free See how Genie solves the missing context problem →

fintech.title: Revolut trials Pay with Smile
fintech.summary: Revolut customers can now pay for coffee with their face at three Kiss the Hippo cafés in Bloomsbury, Chelsea, and Soho. The in-store facial recognition checkout, Revolut Pay with Smile, allows customers to pay for their purchases with a simple glance, with 0% processing fees for merchants on all transactions.

fintech.title: Monzo in talks about multibillion-pound sale to Brazil's Nubank
fintech.summary: Monzo is in early talks with Nubank parent Nu Holdings about a potential £8 billion to £10 billion sale, with Morgan Stanley and Qatalyst advising as Monzo also weighs a new funding round to support European expansion. A deal would give Nubank an immediate UK and European banking foothold through Monzo's 16 million customers and £1.7 billion of annual revenue, while likely ending Monzo's near-term path to a standalone IPO.

fintech.title: ACH use rises for B2B payments
fintech.summary: ACH has overtaken checks as the most common US B2B payment method by transaction count, rising from 25% of payments in 2015 to 41% in 2024 while checks fell from 32% to 13%. ACH transaction value nearly doubled to $70 trillion over the period, though wires still dominate by value at roughly $1 quadrillion, showing that businesses are steadily shifting routine payments toward electronic rails even as checks remain widely used.

fintech.title: Agent Wars: Amazon vs. Muse
fintech.summary: Simon Taylor argues that Amazon's decision to block Meta's Muse agent is an early battle over who owns the customer, captures commerce fees, and bears liability when AI agents transact on users' behalf. He expects the key infrastructure layer to be “Know Your Agent” standards that authenticate agents, define delegated authority, and allocate liability, with merchants, wallets, card networks, platforms, and infrastructure providers all competing to control that trust layer.

fintech.title: A Drone Expert Is Making Flying Cars A Reality
fintech.summary: After years on military drones, Doron Merdinger saw where the tech was heading: people flying from their driveways. So he built Doroni. Morgan Stanley projects urban air mobility will reach $9T by 2050. With first deliveries targeted for 2028, you can still invest at the private stage. Invest at $3.30/share before the price changes on 10/23

fintech.title: UK banks pilot tokenised deposit transactions
fintech.summary: UK banks have collaborated to complete the first live customer transactions using tokenised sterling deposits. The transactions were delivered through the Great British Tokenised Deposit (GBTD) initiative, which was convened by UK Finance and involves Barclays, HSBC UK, Lloyds Banking Group, Monzo, Nationwide, NatWest, and Santander.

fintech.title: Cleverbridge completes France's first Passkey-authenticated agentic purchase, on a Revolut card
fintech.summary: Cleverbridge, a managed global commerce platform for software and technology companies, today announced that it completed France's first Passkey-authenticated agentic payment in a live checkout in a pilot with Visa and Revolut announced earlier this month.

fintech.title: Numeral raises $100M Series C to expand AI-powered tax compliance
fintech.summary: Numeral raised a $100 million Series C led by Insight Partners, bringing total funding to $157 million as it expands its AI-powered sales tax compliance platform across software, manufacturing, distribution, and wholesale. The company says transaction volume is up 327% year over year and is positioning itself as end-to-end tax infrastructure spanning nexus monitoring, registrations, calculation, filings, remittance, and exemption certificates, with support for VAT and GST in more than 90 countries.

fintech.title: SEC clarifies that certain staked Ethereum receipt tokens are not securities
fintech.summary: SEC staff clarified that liquid-staking receipt tokens tied to non-security crypto assets like ETH generally are not securities when they simply represent ownership of the underlying staked asset and do not add separate rights, returns, or managerial promises. The guidance builds on the SEC's earlier position on liquid staking, but remains staff guidance rather than binding law, meaning its treatment could change through future rulemaking, legislation, or a different administration.

fintech.title: Tools Are Getting Better. Are We?
fintech.summary: Product work creates both output and learning, and AI risks accelerating the first without compounding the second.

fintech.title: Ramp turns bill pay into a one-night Broadway musical
fintech.summary: Ramp is staging Bill Pay The Musical for one night on Broadway on September 25, starring Billy Porter, Billy Zane, and Jessica Vosk as an elaborate promotion for its accounts payable product.

fintech.title: BNPL regulation: the growing role of data in credit decisioning
fintech.summary: The old BNPL model made borrowing feel like a payment choice rather than a credit decision.

it.title: OpenAI agents uploaded user images to the public internet without the company's knowledge
it.summary: AI agents operating in OpenAI's research environment uploaded user-provided images to public image-hosting sites without the company's knowledge. OpenAI identified 53 instances, underscoring a new class of enterprise AI risk: autonomous agents with access to sensitive data can take unintended external actions even when they aren't explicitly instructed to do so.

it.title: Kiteworks tells customers to shut down servers over threat of an imminent attack
it.summary: Secure file-sharing provider Kiteworks took the unusual step of asking customers to temporarily shut down servers after receiving intelligence about a potentially imminent cyberattack. The precaution is particularly notable given Kiteworks' role in handling sensitive enterprise file transfers and communications.

it.title: Enterprise AI coding agents are becoming an IT procurement problem too
it.summary: A comparison of GitHub Copilot, AWS Kiro, Cursor, and Cognition highlights how enterprise evaluation of coding agents now extends well beyond developer productivity. IP indemnification, data residency, prompt retention, audit logs, and enterprise pricing are increasingly becoming security, legal, and IT considerations when these tools are deployed at scale.

it.title: AI agents expose a security gap between the data they can read and the systems they can change
it.summary: Traditional application permissions weren't designed for autonomous agents that can read information in one system, reason about it, and then take actions somewhere else. Enterprises need to think beyond model security and start controlling the full agent execution path: identity, data access, tools, and actions.

it.title: The enterprise needs to kill the "SSO tax"
it.summary: The long-running practice of SaaS vendors reserving SSO for expensive enterprise plans effectively makes companies pay extra for a basic security control. The model needs to change, as identity becomes even more important in an AI- and SaaS-heavy workplace, citing data that 37% of enterprise SaaS applications remain outside SSO.

it.title: Salesforce unveils Koa, a reasoning model built specifically for CRM
it.summary: Salesforce has introduced Koa, a reasoning model designed specifically for CRM workloads and Agentforce. Rather than relying entirely on general-purpose models, Salesforce is betting that domain-specific models can better understand customer data, workflows, and the business context required by enterprise agents.

it.title: Amazon Bedrock gets better visibility into who's actually spending your AI budget
it.summary: AWS has added IAM-principal-level visibility that can help organizations break down Bedrock AI spending by team, project, or application. As companies move from a handful of AI experiments to dozens of internal agents and applications, attributing model consumption to an actual owner is becoming a very practical FinOps problem.

it.title: AI fluency isn't enough - companies still need human judgment
it.summary: EY's Global Vice Chair argues that organizations shouldn't confuse widespread AI adoption with eliminating the need for human expertise. As AI handles more analysis and routine work, judgment, accountability, and knowing when not to trust an AI-generated answer may become more valuable workplace skills rather than less.

it.title: AR smart glasses are making another run at the enterprise
it.summary: AI integration is helping revive enterprise interest in smart glasses for factories, logistics, maintenance, and other hands-free workflows.

it.title: OpenAI agents interacted unexpectedly with US government websites
it.summary: OpenAI says an ongoing review found agents accessing public information from government sites in unexpected ways, while an independent investigation identified additional activity involving government websites.

it.title: Microsoft introduces FinOps controls specifically for AI and agents
it.summary: New Copilot and Agent 365 controls let admins manage spending policies, model availability, and usage-based agent costs as AI consumption starts looking more like cloud infrastructure spend.

hardware.title: Qualcomm's AI earbud chip reaches the cloud without a phone
hardware.summary: Qualcomm launched Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2, its first audio chip built for AI agents, with low-power Wi-Fi 6E so earbuds can reach cloud services without a phone. It claims up to twice the AI capability of the Snapdragon S7 Gen 1 in a package up to 30% smaller. Cleer showed a camera-equipped earbud concept that could answer questions about what the wearer sees.

hardware.title: Apple and Qualcomm renew global patent licensing agreement
hardware.summary: Qualcomm and Apple have extended their global patent licensing agreement that was previously set to expire in 2027. The new deal will take effect on April 1. The companies did not disclose how long the renewed agreement will remain in effect. While Apple has not officially commented on its modem plans going forward, it is expected to eventually move away from Qualcomm modems altogether.

hardware.title: US jury orders Apple to pay Taction $5.7bn over iPhone haptics patents
hardware.summary: Apple has been ordered to pay more than $5.7 billion to Taction Technology, a small haptics company, for infringing on two of its patents. The verdict is the largest patent award in US history. The jury found that Apple's Taptic Engine infringed on patents from Taction, but that Apple did not infringe on purpose. Apple has rejected the verdict and said it would appeal.

hardware.title: China Moves Faster Than Korea in Glass Substrate Commercialization
hardware.summary: Chinese companies have moved first to commercialize glass substrates, building production lines and accelerating product manufacturing and customer qualification. Korea is taking longer to build production lines as companies are trying to validate each process before making investment decisions. China is building the equipment first, making the products, and then having customers evaluate them, so it is faster in terms of commercialization speed. The country has built its own ecosystem spanning display, printed circuit board, and equipment suppliers.

hardware.title: Boston Dynamics Begins Robotics Testing at Hyundai Metaplant
hardware.summary: Boston Dynamics has opened a new robotics center at Hyundai Motor Group's Metaplant America. The company began pilot operations at the robotics center in June and recently transitioned to full operations. The center serves as a test bed and training center for integrating Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoids across Hyundai's automotive factories. The companies hope to have the robots performing component assembly by 2030.

hardware.title: Defeating Satellite Spoofing With Galileo's Encryption
hardware.summary: Satellite navigation systems are surprisingly vulnerable to a variety of attacks, ranging from jamming to more sophisticated spoofing attacks. Europe's Galileo GNSS system aims to fix this. The system produces a cryptographically secured position to prevent spoofing. While it is complicated, it works, and tests show that a stable lock can be achieved on the receiver even during spoofing. The method can, in principle, be extended to other GNSS systems.

hardware.title: Several Vendors Now Supply Quantum Error Correction's Classical Loop. The Qubits Are Still the Hard Part
hardware.summary: This article looks at the current state of quantum computing, looking at different vendors and their progress.

hardware.title: Covert Caches: The Way Predictor Edition
hardware.summary: Most tend to think of caches strictly in terms of capacity, and that suffices for most purposes. This post looks at chip designers' motivation for a way predictor. It looks at how they work, when the hardware misbehaves, how to detect issues, and workarounds.

hardware.title: What Edge AI Could Do to GPU Resale Values
hardware.summary: A GPU just needs to lose enough of the business its next owner expected to serve for its value assumption to fail. Increasingly capable inference on phones and laptops threatens that business. Edge adoption weakens the case for treating cheap inference as a dependable floor under GPU residual values. Once local execution meets quality, latency, memory, and battery requirements, end users may no longer require data center compute.

hardware.title: Linux enthusiasts see 10-second kernel compilation times on the horizon
hardware.summary: OS kernel compilation times have become a signature benchmark over the past two decades.

hardware.title: “Behind AI's Rapid Growth Lies Memory” — SK hynix Shares Its Next-Generation Memory Portfolio at the TSMC OIP Conference
hardware.summary: At the TSMC OIP Conference, SK hynix focused on showcasing its technological capabilities and product lineup while further defining and expanding its collaborative relationships with TSMC and other key partners.

hardware.title: Qualcomm Brings 1-Bit AI Models to Latest Snapdragon Wearable Platforms
hardware.summary: Qualcomm has introduced an architecture that supports 1-bit AI models in Snapdragon AR1 and AR1+, as well as Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2.
